devpost_first_sections: Meshtastic is a decentralized off grid communication system using the LoRa peer to peer protocol. It supports direct messaging and private channels. In Amherst, the community is called Pioneer Valley Mesh, and we can connect with CT and NH on a regular basis. Direct messages between two users use the elliptic-curve Diffie-Hellman key exchange algorithm to end-to-end encrypt messages and authenticate messages. Public or private channels, however, rely on a shared secret, which the messages are broadcasted over the network. The primary channel is encrypted with a simple public key known to everyone, which is also used for all periodic broadcasts (position, telemetry, userinfo) by default. Pent

We integrated the secret encryption/decryption algorithm presented in meshmarauder directly into the MeshTNC firmware, allowing for the tool to operate independently. Rather than contact poisoning or modifying incoming packets, we created a convenient CLI tool to construct packets with an arbitrary message and sender. In any channel in which the secret is known, the tool can impersonate any user in a way undetectable to the standard Meshtastic client.

record.problem_and_user: People sharing a physical space are invisible to each other; aimed at strangers in crowded places such as a lecture hall who might meet nearby people.
record.one_line_pitch: Scans nearby Bluetooth devices, shows them as orbiting nodes on a star map, and has GPT-4o-mini write invitation letters that visitors open by scanning a QR code.
record.problem_statement: People in crowded rooms are physically near each other yet invisible and unconnected; the author wanted a consent-first way to surface proximity.
record.devpost_tagline: A consent-first proximity social mesh that maps nearby Bluetooth devices in real-time and uses AI to send handwritten invitation letters to strangers around you.
devpost_first_sections: I was sitting in a packed lecture hall, 200 people around me, every one of them on a device, and zero of us connected to each other. We were surrounded by presence but completely invisible to one another. That moment made me ask: the internet knows every click I've ever made, but it has no idea who I'm physically near right now. GPS gives coordinates. Social media maps followers. But nobody has mapped physical proximity as a human experience. That gap is where X was born.

X - General Intelligence is a consent-first proximity social mesh. It passively senses nearby Bluetooth devices like, phones, laptops, earbuds, displays and visualizes them on a live 2D star map. X sits at the center. Every detected device is a glowing node orbiting by RSSI signal distance. record.what_it_is: A chase game on the hyperbolic plane with five colour layers acting as a fourth dimension. You roll a marble through a maze, phase between layers to pass doors and shake hunters, and looping a pillar shifts layer by itself. An ESP32 tilt controller is optional.
record.problem_and_user: Puzzle and chase-game players, and people curious about hyperbolic geometry; the goal is to let players feel curvature as a mechanic rather than a visual trick.
record.one_line_pitch: Chase game in a hyperbolic maze where a real tilt controller steers and curved space shifts you between colour layers in a 4D-style world.
record.problem_statement: Curved-space games treat curvature as visuals; the author wanted holonomy to be the mechanic, felt physically through a hand controller.
record.devpost_tagline: Roll a marble through a hyperbolic maze where the route you take changes which dimension you're in. Tilt a real controller, slip between 4D layers, and outrun the hunters.
devpost_first_sections: Most "non-Euclidean" games use curved space as a visual trick. I wanted the curvature to be the core mechanic. In curved space, walking around a loop and coming back to where you started still turns you: that's called holonomy. We wanted players to feel that with their hands, by tilting a real controller rather than pressing keys. Perspective puzzles in The Witness and Superliminal inspired the 4D side of the game.

Phase Escape is a chase through a maze built on the hyperbolic plane, a space that curves the opposite way to a sphere. It's drawn in the Poincaré disk, where rooms crowd toward the edge because space grows exponentially. The maze also has a fourth dimension: five layers, each with its own colour. Doors only open in their own colour, shards can only be collected in theirs, and hunters can only see and hurt you when you share their colour. You change layer by twisting the controller like a dial. You can also let space itself do it: roll once around a pillar and you come back one colour over. The four rooms around a pillar form a square with 72° corners instead of 90°, so a lap turns you 360°
